reason: Added two independent real-code levers - the user-config loader silently trims the configured secret, and the digest check hashes it through a charset encoder that replaces an unrepresentable code unit with '?', so a different value collides - and converted the task to the Frontier 1.4 separate-verifier format.

levers.shape: producer off the check's path (config loader): the account's stored secret is trimmed when the deployment's real user configuration is loaded, so the configured trailing character is silently dropped and a different value authenticates over HTTP Basic
levers.skip_reason: the loader is not the login comparison; whitespace around a properties value reads as formatting and the advisory's own fix never touches it
levers.coupled: functional/core/FunctionalConfiguredSecretTest keeps an ordinary and a non-ASCII configured secret authenticating
levers.fairness: Security property: no value other than the exact secret may authenticate, however the account's secret is held; magnitudes: the attack differs by one character the server does not represent faithfully; preservation: the exact configured secret must authenticate

levers.shape: input form the check mishandles: the digest check hashes the configured secret through a charset encoder whose replacement action maps an unpaired surrogate onto '?', so a different presented value hashes to the same bytes and authenticates
levers.skip_reason: after the representation is corrected to UTF-8 the comparison looks exact; only malformed-Unicode secrets are affected, which a deployment is not expected to configure
levers.coupled: functional/core/FunctionalUnrepresentableNeighbourTest keeps a valid supplementary-character secret authenticating; FunctionalDigestEncodingTest keeps ordinary non-ASCII secrets authenticating
levers.fairness: Security property: no value other than the exact secret may authenticate, however the value is presented; magnitudes: the attack differs by one character the server does not represent faithfully

fail_confidence_reason: Two independent HOW-type traps survive an ISO-8859-1-to-UTF-8 sweep and target the two documented model failure modes (a dismissible config-loader path and an encoder input shape), so a run that fixes one still fails the other, and the coupled functional values punish the over-broad fixes MiMo tends to make.
